content.text:
Let me analyze. I'm Greyjoy, round 6, 4 victory points (4 castle areas, 2 strongholds... wait it says castles:4, strongholds:2, landAreas:5? Actually controlledCastleAreas 4). I have 2 knights in Moat Cailin (units 6 and 37).

Options from Moat Cailin: greywater-watch (mine), seagard (mine), the-twins (neutral, no castle), white-harbor (neutral, castle=1, capture gains 1 castle area without combat), winterfell (stark, garrison 2, footman defended, defense +1).

White Harbor is a castle, controlled by no one (controller null). Moving there gains a castle area = victory point 5 for me. No combat. Great.

Winterfell: defended by Stark footman (id 33), garrison 2, Defense +1 order. Attacking with 2 knights = 4 strength. Defender: footman 1 + garrison 2 + defense +1 = 4. Plus support: Stark has support orders at Castle Black (2 knights = 4 strength), Karhold (1 knight = 2), and Greyjoy support at greywater-watch. Wait, but Stark supports... Castle Black adjacent to Winterfell? Winterfell neighbours: bay-of-ice, castle-black, karhold, moat-cailin, port-of-winterfell, the-shivering-sea, the-stony-shore, white-harbor. Yes castle-black and karhold adjacent. So Stark could support Winterfell with 4+2=6 strength. That's way too much. Attacker 4 base +1? march +0. Plus Greyjoy support from greywater-watch (footman 1). So 5. Stark defense 4 + 6 support = 10. Impossible.

So attacking Winterfell is bad. White Harbor is a free castle.

But wait, can I reach white-harbor with both knights? Yes. White Harbor has no units, no garrison? Let me check: white-harbor [land; castle=1]: moat-cailin, port-of-white-harbor, the-narrow-sea, the-shivering-sea, widows-watch, winterfell. Controller null. So capturing gives me a castle area with no combat.

But note: The-narrow-sea has a Stark ship (id 4). White Harbor is adjacent to the-narrow-sea. Stark ship in the narrow sea could raid? No, raids already resolved. But Stark ship with no order.

Actually wait, moving into white-harbor: no combat. Good. That gains me 1 castle area → 5 victory points.

Should I leave a power token at Moat Cailin? Moat Cailin is a castle (castle=1), contributes 1 castle area. If I move both knights out, I lose control unless I place a power token. I have 8 power tokens. Spend 1 to keep Moat Cailin. That's essential - losing a castle would negate the gain.

So: move both knights to white-harbor, leave_power_token true.

Actually, should I split? Move one knight to white-harbor and one stays? No, need at least one to capture. Two knights in white harbor forms an army of 2 - supply check: supply 3, permitted army sizes 3,2,2,2. So army of 2 is fine. Moat Cailin empty, place power token.

Wait but actually maybe consider: moving only one knight, leaving one at Moat Cailin, no need for power token. But then Moat Cailin still controlled (has unit). And white harbor gains castle. That keeps 8 power tokens. But then white harbor has 1 knight = single unit, no supply concern. And Moat Cailin has 1 knight (single unit).

Hmm, which is better? Leaving a knight in Moat Cailin defends it. But moving both and leaving power token: Moat Cailin defended only by power token (no units) — vulnerable to attack. Actually Moat Cailin is mine and could be attacked. Leaving a unit is better defense.

Actually think about threats: Who can attack Moat Cailin? Adjacent: greywater-watch (mine), seagard (mine), the-narrow-sea (stark ship), the-twins (neutral), white-harbor, winterfell. Stark could march from... Winterfell through? Not adjacent to Moat Cailin? Winterfell is adjacent to Moat Cailin. Stark has footman at Winterfell. Could attack with footman + support from castle-black (knights). But that's a stretch.

Better to keep a defender? But leaving one knight means only one knight captures white-harbor — still fine, single unit.

Hmm, but is there value in a bigger army at white-harbor? White harbor could face counterattack from Winterfell or the-narrow-sea. Actually Stark footman at Winterfell could march to White Harbor. If I have 2 knights there, defense stronger.

Let me think about the strongest play. I want to gain White Harbor (castle). Preserve Moat Cailin.

Option A: both knights to white-harbor, leave power token at Moat Cailin. Cost 1 power. Moat Cailin undefended.
Option B: one knight to white-harbor, one stays at Moat Cailin. No power cost. Both areas controlled by units.

Option B seems better - keeps both areas controlled, no power cost, and both have a unit. White Harbor single knight though. Actually wait - if a single knight at Moat Cailin, it can still be attacked. But at least it's a defender.

Hmm, but actually there's a subtlety: supply. Option A puts army of 2 at white harbor - fine. Option B: single units each.

Actually, could the march to white-harbor plus knight at Moat Cailin matter for future? Having a knight at Moat Cailin could march next round too. 

Actually, let me reconsider: is capturing White Harbor worth it vs. keeping both knights at Moat Cailin to defend? White Harbor gives +1 victory point, putting me at 5. That's good progress. Lannister at 4, Martell at 3.

I'll go with moving both knights to white-harbor and leaving a power token? Or one knight?

Let me consider defense of White Harbor more. If I move both, White Harbor has 2 knights. Stark might counterattack. But it's a castle now mine.

Actually the safest strong move: move one knight to white-harbor (capture, gain castle), keep one at Moat Cailin (defends the castle there without spending power). This nets +1 castle area, controls both, no power spent. 

But wait, having a lone knight at Moat Cailin vs a power token—the power token is more exposed. But actually keeping a unit at Moat Cailin is good.

Hmm, but consider: With one knight at Moat Cailin and one at White Harbor, both are single units. If White Harbor gets attacked by Stark, a single knight defends at 2+... but no defense order there.

Alternatively moving both keeps a stronger force at the newly won castle which is the more forward/valuable position.

Let me think about what maximizes victory. Both options gain White Harbor. Difference is defense allocation and 1 power token.

I think keeping the knight at Moat Cailin (Option B) is more conservative and preserves power. But Moat Cailin is a rear area, less likely attacked. White Harbor is forward, more likely contested.

Actually the biggest threat to White Harbor: Stark. Stark has 2 knights at Castle Black (support only), 1 knight at Karhold (support), 1 footman at Winterfell. Stark's March orders? Only Winterfell has Defense. The-narrow-sea has no order (removed). Stark has no march orders revealed except... none. So Stark can't attack this round! Their only march-relevant units have support/defense/consolidate orders. So White Harbor is safe this round.

Therefore moving both knights to White Harbor is safe, and White Harbor is more valuable to hold with 2 knights. But I'd need a power token at Moat Cailin.

Alternatively move both, and... actually I could leave one knight at Moat Cailin to avoid the power cost. But Moat Cailin isn't threatened this round either (Stark has no march orders). So no urgency to defend either.

Hmm. Given no immediate threat, gain White Harbor and keep both controlled. To keep both controlled with both knights moved, need power token (1 power). 8 power is plenty.

Actually, is it better to leave one knight at Moat Cailin than spend a power token? Power tokens are valuable for future bids and control. 8 is a lot, and I have strong lead on power. Spending 1 is fine.

But hold on — I could also move both knights and NOT leave a token, losing Moat Cailin (a castle). That would net 0. No.

Decision: Move both knights (6, 37) to white-harbor, leave_power_token true.

Wait, but is it legal to have both go to one destination? Yes.

Actually let me reconsider whether moving only to white harbor and leaving Moat Cailin with the token. Since both knights moved, Moat Cailin has no units but a power token preserves control. Good.

Alternatively, keep it simpler: move both knights to white-harbor. That's the plan.

Hmm, but what about the possibility of splitting: one knight to white harbor (capture), one to the-twins? The-twins is neutral, no castle, no gain. Not useful.

So final: moves = [{destination_region_id: "white-harbor", unit_ids: [6,37]}], leave_power_token: true.

Let me double check supply: army of 2 knights at white harbor, supply 3 permits 3,2,2,2. Fine.

Also check: does moving to White Harbor create any issue with the other knight? No.

Let me verify White Harbor control: controller null means no power token of any house, no units. Good, no combat.

I'll submit.

Let me quickly check neighbours of white-harbor to confirm no enemy units there. Actually the observation already lists white-harbor: controller null, units []. Good.

I'll just submit. Maybe one tool call to confirm white-harbor. Not necessary. Let me just answer.

Actually let me be careful about the leave_power_token mechanic: "This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established." Since both units leave, and I can establish control (Moat Cailin is a land area I control), true.

Final answer.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

leave_power_token.description: Spend one available power token to preserve control when legally vacating the source area. This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established.
leave_power_token.title: Leave Power Token

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
